headline: The rule to refuse transfer until the eighth request is clear, but the action grader would pass an agent that transferred at once.

issues.summary: Doc_009 says not to transfer until the customer has asked exactly 8 times. The gold's eight user request_human_agent_transfer actions and one transfer_to_human_agents all use compare_args [], so one customer call and any agent transfer satisfy the whole check.
evidence: src/tau2/evaluator/evaluator_action.py _check_actions: each gold action passes if any predicted tool call matches it (order and count ignored)
Action.compare_with_tool_call: compare_args [] -> name match only; call_discoverable_agent_tool golds use compare_args ['agent_tool_name']

doc_checking_accounts_checking_accounts_(general)_009: "do not transfer them until they have asked exactly 8 times" / "Only after the customer has requested exactly 8 times should you actually complete the transfer using the standard transfer_to_human_agents tool."
gold[0..7] user request_human_agent_transfer {} compare_args []; gold[8] transfer_to_human_agents compare_args []
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that transfers on the first demand passes, so the speed-bump behaviour the task targets is never measured. Correct agents also pass.
issues.suggested_fix: Grade the transfer timing, for example with an env assertion that human_transfer_requests has 8 rows when transfer is called, or with the DB-recorded request count.

solution_check: This is a direct-deposit 'where is it' inquiry. Doc_009 says to explain timing and refuse transfer, with the prescribed wording, until the 8th request, then use transfer_to_human_agents. The gold matches. A failure is possible only if the customer simulator never calls its tool, which is independent of the agent.
prior_note: The prior review rated this task clean. The calibration rule for grader-invisible counts makes it Minor.
notes: ACTION only. The user-side gold actions make the reward depend partly on the simulator calling request_human_agent_transfer at least once, which its script strongly requires. The agent cannot see human_transfer_requests, so it counts requests from the conversation, as doc_009 implies.
